head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Support K=64 `tcgen05.mma` instructions for dense block-scaled FP8 MMA on sm_107f.

On sm_107f, dense block-scaled 8-bit floating-point `tcgen05.mma` can consume K=64 per instruction instead of K=32, for instructions with M=128 (1 CTA) or M=256 (2 CTAs). Use K=64 steps in that case, so that fewer instructions are issued, as is already done for the non-scaled variant.

display_title: fix(random): preserve truncated normal bound dtypes

head_commit.message:
fix(random): preserve truncated normal bound dtypes

The infinities passed to lax.nextafter were created with NumPy arrays, which canonicalize to float32 when x64 is disabled even when explicit float64 dtypes are allowed. Build them from the corresponding bounds so truncated_normal keeps matching dtypes. This fixes the float64 truncated_normal call under jax_explicit_x64_dtypes=allow.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Return False from jnp.array_equiv when same-rank shapes are unbroadcastable

head_commit.message:
Catch TypeError in jnp.array_equiv when shapes cannot be broadcast

Fixes #42873

When two same-rank input arrays have incompatible shapes for broadcasting (e.g. (2,) and (3,)), lax.eq raises a TypeError rather than a ValueError. Previously, array_equiv only caught ValueError, causing a TypeError to escape instead of returning False as required by NumPy semantics.

This commit catches (ValueError, TypeError) in array_equiv and adds a regression test case.

Signed-off-by: Manoj Jana <jm2705470@gmail.com>

display_title: Reimplemented `gpu_info` using `jaxlib._gpu_spec`

head_commit.message:
Reimplemented `gpu_info` using `jaxlib._gpu_spec`

The vast majority of the diff is from #39469 by vfdev-5@.

A few things to highlight:

* The GPUs available for AOT are limited to the XLA GPU specs, and the
  abstract device kind has to match one of a spec's registered device
  descriptions exactly, e.g. "NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3" rather than "NVIDIA H100".
* `registry` is removed, so there is no way to register a custom `GpuTargetConfig`.
* For the local GPU, `get_gpu_info` returns the matching XLA spec when one
  exists and falls back to building a config from the device's attributes on
  the fly otherwise.
* There is no public API for this feature yet.

Merging this change closes #39469

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [lax] Fix ragged_dot nan from inf in another group's rhs

head_commit.message:
[lax] Fix ragged_dot nan from inf in another group's rhs

Fixes #42918.

`lax.ragged_dot` zeroed `lhs` outside each group and contracted over
the group axis, so every row picked up a `0 * rhs[g]` term from every
other group. When `rhs[g]` holds an `inf` that term is `nan`,
corrupting unrelated rows (and rows in no group). Dot the unmasked
`lhs` against every group's `rhs` in one batched dot, then select each
row's own group's result; rows in no group select nothing and sum to
zero. Adds regression tests with the issue's repro, for a narrow
`group_sizes` dtype, and for exporting with a symbolic ragged extent.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: Fix hyp2f1 hanging for large |a| (float loop counter in the terminating series)

head_commit.message:
Fix hyp2f1 hanging for large |a| (float loop counter in the terminating series)

_hyp2f1_terminal is evaluated for every input (all branches go through
select_n) and looped with a floating-point index up to |a| + 1. Once the
index passes the largest integer the dtype counts exactly (2048 for float16,
2**24 for float32), i + 1 == i and the loop never ends. Use an integer trip
count that is 0 unless the terminating branch is the selected one.

Fixes #42939

display_title: Fix dot_product_attention XLA backend returning NaN on all-masked rows

head_commit.message:
Fix dot_product_attention XLA backend returning NaN on all-masked rows

When attention logits contain a fully masked row (all -inf, such as from additive bias in padded sequences), standard softmax evaluates exp(-inf - (-inf)) = exp(NaN) = NaN.

In contrast, cuDNN sdpa produces 0.0 without NaNs for all-masked rows.

This commit updates _dot_product_attention_core in the XLA backend to replace -inf in logits_max with 0.0 and safely zero out probabilities when probs_sum == 0, matching cuDNN behavior and returning 0.0 with clean gradients. Also avoids triggering FloatingPointError under jax.debug_infs(True).

Fixes #42929.

Signed-off-by: Manoj Jana <jm2705470@gmail.com>

head_commit.message:
Improve precision of `jax.scipy.special.kl_div` in the near-one regime (`0.5 < p / q < 2`) using an `atanh`-based series in `s = (p - q) / (p + q)`, restoring full float64 precision and avoiding cancellation in bfloat16/float16 near the branch boundary.

name: Bazel CUDA
display_title: [Pallas TPU] Preserve enclosing named scopes inside nested kernel regions.

head_commit.message:
[Pallas TPU] Preserve enclosing named scopes inside nested kernel regions.

Sub-jaxprs are traced with a reset name stack, so their equations only record
the scopes opened inside the region body. Mosaic TPU lowering computed the
full `eqn_name_stack` for the equation location but passed the unchanged
context to the lowering rule, so ops inside `pl.when`, `pl.loop`,
`pl.run_scoped`, `lax.cond`/`switch`, `lax.fori_loop`/`while_loop`/`scan`,
`custom_jvp`/`custom_vjp`, `emit_pipeline` and SparseCore `parallel_loop`
lost every enclosing `jax.named_scope`.

This change:

* Sets `eqn_name_stack` on the lowering context while the rule runs (and
  restores it afterwards), so nested regions inherit the enclosing scopes.
  The rule keeps using the same context object, so accumulator allocation
  and trace ops are unchanged.
* Lowers cached functions and unrolled loop bodies with an empty name stack
  and an unknown location, and cached functions under a reset source-info
  context (new `source_info_util.reset_source_info()`), so they no longer
  capture the scopes or traceback of the first callsite; each callsite adds
  its own location when the function is inlined. The lowering-cache key is
  unchanged.
* Forwards the scopes enclosing `emit_pipeline` to the kernel lowered by the
  compiler pipeline emitter.
